Research Prompt: Comparable Projects to a Collaborative Crypto+AI Browser Desktop Environment

I need you to research whether any projects exist that are comparable to — or overlap significantly with — a system called "Slop Computer." Below are its core technical components. For each, find any existing tools, protocols, open-source projects, or products that do something similar, and note how closely they match.

Component 1 — Multiplayer Browser Desktop / Shared OS Environment Find projects that create a shared, collaborative desktop experience inside a browser — where multiple remote users can see and interact with the same desktop state simultaneously (shared filesystem, shared apps, synchronized UI). Not just screen sharing — actual shared state with multi-cursor support.

Component 2 — Server-Side Co-Browsing with Stealth/Anti-Bot Bypass Find tools or open-source projects that run a headless browser on a backend server and stream its visual output to multiple clients in real time, while routing participant input back. Specifically interested in any that attempt to bypass anti-bot protections (Cloudflare, fingerprinting) to access sites that block automation. Puppeteer-stealth, noVNC, and similar are relevant starting points.

Component 3 — Ethereum Transaction Interception / Fake Provider Injection Find any tools that inject a custom window.ethereum provider into a browser session to intercept pending transactions before they execute — routing raw transaction data to external participants rather than broadcasting to chain. This is distinct from simulation tools like Tenderly — I'm looking for live interception during real browsing sessions.

Component 4 — Collaborative Multisig with Dynamic Deployment Find any systems where a multisig smart contract is deployed dynamically per-session, pending transactions are surfaced to a group UI for threshold signing, and execution only happens after quorum — specifically in the context of a shared browsing or collaborative dapp interaction session, not just a standard Safe/Gnosis setup.

Component 5 — Censorship-Resistant Live Streaming with IPFS Frontend Find projects that combine self-hosted RTMP ingest (e.g., MediaMTX or similar) with WebRTC/HLS distribution, where the viewer frontend is a static app pinned to IPFS and accessible via ENS. Livepeer is a known comparable — how close does it get to this full stack?

Component 6 — SIWE + Password Hybrid Auth for Mixed Audiences Find any live collaboration or streaming tools that support both wallet-based authentication (SIWE) and a non-crypto fallback (password/invite link) for the same session, where wallet-connected users get elevated capabilities (e.g., cursor identity, transaction signing).

Synthesis Ask: After covering each component, give me your assessment of whether any single project combines 3 or more of these components together. If nothing matches the full combination, say so clearly. Flag any projects that are in active development vs. abandoned. Include GitHub links, dates of last activity, and any known team/org affiliation where available.

Protocol: PMFI OpLend V2.2

Network: Base Mainnet, chain ID 8453

Application:
https://oplend.pmfi.cc/

Verified core contracts:

1. PMFIPositionFactoryV22 / core position creation
0xb2458426F7263B3Aec44ba6E3466bB4B5A175ccf

Verified source:
https://basescan.org/address/0xb2458426F7263B3Aec44ba6E3466bB4B5A175ccf#code

2. PMFIPrimaryMarketplaceV22 / primary lender marketplace
0xcC3E1C18b58eE8Ec6550C60b75d820E4b45e2D2F

Verified source:
https://basescan.org/address/0xcC3E1C18b58eE8Ec6550C60b75d820E4b45e2D2F#code

Please audit both contracts as one connected system. The marketplace is part of the security-critical funding and accounting flow and should not be excluded from the factory review.

PROTOCOL OVERVIEW

OpLend is an option-based collateral funding primitive rather than a conventional overcollateralized loan.

A borrower locks an allowlisted ERC-20 collateral asset and chooses:

- collateral amount;
- target USDC to raise;
- total fixed USDC repayment;
- funding deadline;
- repayment deadline.

The factory creates an isolated position vault and associated P and N position tokens.

The borrower initially owns the position claims. P-side inventory is offered to lenders through the primary marketplace. Lenders fund the position with USDC by purchasing P exposure.

The borrower retains the N-side position.

There is:

- no price oracle used for settlement;
- no health factor;
- no price-based liquidation;
- no automatic liquidation;
- no variable debt balance;
- no claim against the borrower’s unrelated wallet assets.

SETTLEMENT OUTCOMES

1. Borrower repays

The borrower must complete the fixed USDC repayment required for the funded portion before the repayment deadline.

Partial repayment does not unlock collateral.

After complete repayment:

- P holders receive their proportional USDC repayment;
- the borrower can recover the accounted collateral through the relevant N-side settlement path.

2. Borrower does not repay

After the repayment deadline:

- P holders receive proportional claims on the accounted collateral;
- the borrower keeps the USDC raised during funding;
- the borrower loses the collateral backing the funded position;
- no additional wallet debt is created.

3. Partial funding

Only the funded portion becomes economically active.

Example:

- target raise: 1,000 USDC;
- amount funded: 300 USDC.

The borrower’s repayment obligation is calculated from the funded portion, not from the entire 1,000 USDC target.

Please verify the exact proportional repayment, unsold-position, refund and close-funding accounting across the factory, vault and marketplace.

IMPORTANT ACCOUNTING MODEL

The protocol intentionally distinguishes raw ERC-20 balances from internally accounted assets.

Relevant concepts include:

- accountedCollateral;
- tracked collateral settlement pools;
- tracked USDC settlement pools;
- funded P inventory;
- unsold P inventory;
- borrower collateral/refund claims;
- lender USDC or collateral claims.

Direct token transfers or donations to a vault must not create additional protocol claims.

A raw balance such as:

collateral.balanceOf(vault)

may be greater than:

vault.accountedCollateral()

This difference is intentional when unsolicited tokens have been transferred to the vault.

P/N supply, marketplace inventory, repayment calculations, lender recovery and borrower refunds must be based only on internally accounted amounts—not on unsolicited raw balances.

PREDICTABLE-ADDRESS PREFUNDING INVARIANT

A future CREATE vault address may be predictable, and an external account may transfer collateral to that address before the vault is deployed.

The intended invariant is:

- prefunding must not block legitimate position creation;
- prefunding must not increase accountedCollateral;
- prefunding must not increase P supply;
- prefunding must not increase N supply;
- prefunding must not increase marketplace sale inventory;
- prefunding must not increase borrower refund rights;
- prefunding must not increase lender default recovery;
- later collateral or USDC donations must not generate claims.

This scenario has a dedicated regression suite:

PMFIOpLendingV22PrefundRegressionTest

Passing tests:

- test_PrefundDoesNotBlockCreationOrMintExtraClaims
- test_DonationDoesNotIncreaseDefaultRecovery
- test_DonationDoesNotIncreaseBorrowerRefundClaim

Latest focused result:

3 passed
0 failed
0 skipped

Please independently reproduce and validate these properties rather than assuming the tests are sufficient.

MARKETPLACE ACCOUNTING

Please review the complete primary-sale lifecycle, including:

- P inventory registered for sale;
- partial fills;
- cumulative rather than per-fill pricing;
- rounding across multiple purchases;
- maximum sellable inventory;
- sold versus unsold P accounting;
- USDC received from lenders;
- protocol sale fees;
- closing funding;
- refunds or collateral corresponding to unsold inventory;
- prevention of double purchase or double claim;
- handling of fee-on-transfer or non-standard USDC behavior;
- marketplace registration failure or denial-of-service;
- whether a compromised or paused marketplace can block new positions;
- whether a vault can be registered more than once;
- whether arbitrary or fake vaults can be registered.

SECURITY DESIGN

- Contracts are non-upgradeable.
- No delegatecall-based upgrade path is intended.
- Collateral uses a strict owner-managed allowlist.
- Permissionless collateral mode is not intended.
- The protocol uses immutable Base USDC:
  0x833589fCD6eDb6E08f4c7C32D4f71b54bdA02913
- USDC uses 6 decimals.
- Collateral token decimals may vary.
- Position-token accounting must remain correct across different collateral decimals.
- Creation fee: 0.0001 ETH.
- Primary marketplace sale fee: 10 basis points, or 0.1%.
- Reentrancy guards, checks-effects-interactions and exact transfer-delta checks are intended for relevant external-token flows.
- Pausing is intended to stop creation of new risk while preserving user exit and settlement paths.
- Ownership uses a two-step transfer process.
- Administrative control is held by:
  0x7C8d9ad4F51299b02755Ec13C018004008b45494

Please verify every statement above against the verified deployed source rather than treating it as an assumption.

POSITION TOKEN DESIGN

P represents the lender-facing claim.

Depending on settlement, P should produce either:

- proportional USDC after complete borrower repayment; or
- proportional accounted collateral after default.

N represents the borrower-side residual claim.

N transfer restrictions are intentional in V2.2. Please still assess:

- whether restrictions can lock legitimate settlement;
- loss-of-wallet consequences;
- whether transfer restrictions can be bypassed;
- interactions between P/N supply and pair redemption;
- whether P and N can be burned, redeemed or exercised more than once;
- whether token transfers during funding can break marketplace accounting.

PRIMARY AUDIT PRIORITIES

Please prioritize:

1. Factory-to-marketplace cross-contract assumptions.
2. Position creation and initialization.
3. Predictable-address prefunding.
4. Unsolicited collateral and USDC donations.
5. Accounted balances versus raw ERC-20 balances.
6. Partial funding.
7. Cumulative pricing over multiple partial fills.
8. Full-repayment enforcement.
9. Default settlement.
10. Borrower refund and unsold-collateral accounting.
11. P and N minting, burning and redemption.
12. Independent claimCollateral and claimUsdc paths.
13. Double claims and repeated settlement.
14. Rounding and residual dust, especially 18-decimal collateral claims against 6-decimal USDC.
15. Final-redeemer handling.
16. Funding and repayment deadline boundaries.
17. Zero-length or impractically short repayment windows.
18. Fee-on-transfer, rebasing, callback and malicious ERC-20 collateral.
19. Reentrancy and external-call ordering.
20. Marketplace notification or registration failure.
21. Pause behavior and availability of exits while paused.
22. Owner/Safe powers and centralization risks.
23. Allowlist additions and removals during active positions.
24. Exact versus excess creation-fee handling.
25. Protocol fee withdrawal accounting.
26. Vault authenticity and verified-vault checks.
27. Denial-of-service and griefing attacks.
28. CREATE address prediction and nonce assumptions.
29. Solvency invariants under arbitrary operation ordering.
30. Any discrepancy between emitted events, stored accounting and actual asset balances.

IMPORTANT REQUEST REGARDING PREVIOUS PREFUNDING ANALYSIS

Do not infer an economic claim solely from a vault’s raw ERC-20 balance.

When examining a prefunded or donated vault, separately compare:

- raw collateral balance;
- accountedCollateral;
- P total supply;
- N total supply;
- marketplace registered inventory;
- funded amount;
- tracked collateral pool;
- tracked USDC pool;
- borrower refund credit;
- aggregate lender claim.

A finding should demonstrate that unsolicited assets alter one of the internally accounted claims, not only that they appear in balanceOf(vault).

Please decode createPosition calldata using the verified V2.2 ABI and struct layout rather than a reconstructed flat function signature.

EXPECTED CORE INVARIANTS

- P total supply and N total supply must not exceed protocol-accounted collateral except where an explicitly documented burn or settlement state explains the difference.
- Unsolicited transfers must create no borrower or lender claims.
- Total USDC claimed must not exceed tracked USDC available for claims.
- Total collateral claimed must not exceed tracked collateral available for claims.
- A user must not claim both mutually exclusive settlement outcomes for the same position.
- Complete repayment must be required before borrower collateral recovery.
- Default must not create additional debt beyond the locked collateral.
- Partial funding must not create repayment obligations for the unfunded target.
- Sum of sold and unsold P accounting must remain consistent with issued inventory.
- Sale fees must not be included as lender principal or borrower repayment.
- Closing funding, repayment and default settlement must each be single-use state transitions.
- Pausing must not trap already-earned user claims.
- Only factory-created, authenticated vaults should enter the marketplace.
- No unsupported collateral should be accepted at position creation.
- Admin changes should not retroactively corrupt active-position accounting.

Please provide:

- reproducible proof-of-concept tests for each confirmed finding;
- exact affected functions and state transitions;
- assumptions required for exploitability;
- maximum realistic financial impact;
- whether a finding affects existing positions, only future positions, or only availability;
- differentiation between intentional design choices and exploitable security issues.
